claims: n-228-candidate.yaml is a packing.squares:Witness/v2 file (corners, rational scalars, 228 squares) whose exact rational side, rounded up at 12 places, #983 prints as the bound, 15.600801734812; the issue and README also print the exact side as 15.6008017348117538028514559173910014808630264..., and sqcheck-228.txt prints it rounded up at 15 places, 15.600801734811754. Its exact coordinates were produced by this repository's packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational at fa980f8e from the lab's decimal pose, n-228-decimal-pose.yaml, with center_dilation '1' and no dilation; translating the least corner coordinates to zero and taking the greatest corner extent as the side lowered the pose's side by about 2.04e-13, which the issue calls normalization and not part of the 0.0038 gain. The decimal pose was certified in interval arithmetic by sqcheck.py at its own side, pair margin at least 2.02e-13 and wall margin at least 1.01e-13. An upper bound only: no optimality, KKT or rigidity claim.

n228-witness.json is the same witness as JSON. verify-228.txt is the author's unmodified run of this repository's packing-witness verify at fa980f8e (VERIFIED, exact-algebraic over Q, 25878 pairs); checks/registry.json reports the same run's least best pair gap, exactly 101/500000000000000, and least wall clearance, 0. sqcheck-228.txt is the author's run of verifier/sqcheck.py, an exact checker the source says was implemented separately (VALID, exact rational, the exact side rounded up at 15 places). checks/promote.json, checks/exact.json and checks/interval.json are the promotion's report and sqcheck.py's JSON reports on the exact witness and on the decimal pose. The issue says promotion shares code with packing-witness verify and that sqcheck.py is separate. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.

The issue and README say the packing is an original AI-run column-band proposal design (the lab's Sol near1 director, gpt-6.1-sol), not a donor or transplant start or a public recovery: axis-parallel squares occupy two wall-anchored staircase or corner domains, tilted stacks span a diagonal band, and a finite-memory dynamic programme over the columns generates proposals, with no global count optimality asserted for arbitrary-angle junctions. Full emitted-count and far-overlap audits precede one quench with Evan Daniel's ALM+SLP fq optimizer from evand/square-packing search/packer, built from bb4cc78e, MIT; no random kicks were used for this hit. hit-n228-114-0.txt is the filed hit, of kind design, from the proposal f = 0.596543, delta 1 degree, tolerance 0.03, count 228, 48 tilted squares, column offset 0.026742, variant 1, corner layout t:4,4, final decimal side 15.60080173481195764 at 121 seconds of search; hit-n228-114-0.json records that metadata. They say the final packing has 50 squares tilted beyond 0.5 degree against the record's 51, and, against the registry packing matched up to the square's eight symmetries, that all 228 centres move by more than 0.001, 93 by more than 0.05 (largest 0.940), and 59 squares retilt by more than 1 degree. The issue names the record s(228) <= 15.60460147572967429 (Francisco Couzo, improved by PingYou Ltd, 2026-10-13) and the gain on it, 0.00379974091792048 by exact Fraction comparison, relative 2.435e-4. It states first a side-only Kaggle leaderboard entry at 228, 15.596043116646 (square1000, 29 October, cache of 9 November 20:52 UTC), 0.004758618166 below this side, which this packing does not beat and which supplies no packing; and it quotes the best public Kaggle packing it found, 15.604601475744 (kirilltym, data of 11 November), above this side. They ask that Doğa Özden be recorded as found_by for this new arrangement, that the old record stay credited to Francisco Couzo and PingYou Ltd, and that Evan Daniel be credited for the optimizer. The issue says search, checks and filing were AI-assisted throughout, and that the issue and repository were prepared and posted on Özden's behalf by his AI agent, which uses the account kenaznia-doga.
